src: Quad-City Times (Davenport), 9 Aug 1911, p. 2, 'Farmer Finds $3,050 in Gold' (Newspapers.com 299719240)

set.n: John Meade's gold in baking-powder cans, old shed on the Meade farm near Iowa City (found 1911)
set.st: In August 1911 T. T. Meade, a wealthy farmer of 570 acres six miles from Iowa City, found $3,050 in $10 and $20 gold pieces in five small baking-powder cans while tearing down an old shed. His father John Meade, who died about 1907, had habitually hidden gold 'about the buildings of the farm'; the latest coin was dated 1899. The Oskaloosa Herald's version puts the farm nine miles east of town. Found 1911; no further find reported. Pin is the town, not the farm.
set.tovw: Lead grade F: $3,050 recovered in 1911 (two accounts); the father's habit of hiding gold about the buildings leaves a possibility, not a record, of more
set.t: Recovered 1911. If the Meade farm turns up on the 1917 Johnson Co plat, the other outbuilding sites are the only open question. Private: permission.
set.pl: Meade farm 6-9 mi from Iowa City, direction unsettled; not yet on a plat
pinev: Quad-City Times: 'six miles from Iowa City', no direction; Oskaloosa Herald: 'nine miles east of town'. 1910 census has only a John Meade b. 1872 in Clear Creek Twp (W of town), a poor match. The 1917 Johnson Co plat is the next check.
Iowa Populated Places point for Iowa City (41.6611, -91.5302); r15000 so the ring reaches both the 6-mile and the 9-mile readings.

Atlas of Warren County, Iowa (Hovey & Frame 1902) p.6, UIowa Digital Library atlases_11282; research/plats/ogle-medora-warren-1902.md
pinev: 1902 Warren Co atlas p.6 (Squaw Twp, T74N R24W) shows F. M. Ogle's 80 acres in the S part of sec 10 with a house dot; pin on the house, about 4 km N of Medora (the plate prints Medora in sec 27). Supersedes the 1940-atlas family-land centre. Pin confidence B (plat-placed).

The Register puts the home 'southwest of Indianola' in 'a small shanty and dugout on his farm', the estate guessed as high as $250,000, burial at Hewitt cemetery; 'much speculation is made as to where his wealth is hid'. Consistent with the sec 10 Squaw Twp house.
